title: Miss Huangshan's Last Cable Car and It's 10,000 Steps Down | China Travel Expert
description:
Miss the last cable car down Huangshan and the only way off the mountain is on foot — thousands of stone steps, in the dark.

Huangshan (Yellow Mountain) in Anhui is a sea of granite peaks, twisted pines and cloud. The whole range is paved with more than 60,000 stone steps, and a full peak-to-peak traverse runs 10,000+ steps with roughly 2,700 m of cumulative climbing — even fit hikers take 10–12 hours. Three cableways (Yungu, Yuping, Taiping) carry you up for about ¥80–90 one way, but they stop running in the late afternoon. If you summit late and miss the last car, the descent is on foot. Peak-season entry (Mar 1–Nov 30) is ¥190.

🧭 Expert Tip: the moment you arrive, check that day's last cable-car time at the station — it shifts with season and weather — and start down with a buffer, or book a summit hotel and descend the next morning.
